exam.subject: History
exam.title: Warsay Yikealo Secondary School, Sawa History Department Second Semester Final (Model) Examination, 2014/15

questions.stem: The period from the fall of Western Roman empire ($$ 476 \text{ AD} $$) to $$ 15^{th} \text{ C AD} $$ is known as:
explanation_steps: The **Middle Ages** (or Medieval period) is the era in European history that followed the fall of the Western Roman Empire in $$ 476 \text{ AD} $$ and lasted until the beginning of the Renaissance in the $$ 15^{th} \text{ century} $$.

questions.stem: The Kingdom of Bunyoro-Kitara was set up by:
explanation_steps: The **Bacwezi** (or Backwesi) are legendary figures in the Great Lakes region of Africa who are credited with establishing the Empire of Kitara, the predecessor to the Bunyoro kingdom.

questions.stem: The Opium War of 1839 was completed with the **Treaty of Nanking**. Identify the statement that is **not** among the points of the treaty.

options.B: Hong-Kong to be given to British.
options.C: Britain’s legal right to have jurisdiction over its citizens in China.
options.D: Canton to be given to France.

explanation_steps: The Treaty of Nanking (1842) was between Britain and China. It ceded Hong Kong to Britain, opened five treaty ports (including Canton), and established extraterritoriality (British jurisdiction over its citizens). Canton was opened for trade, not given to France.

questions.stem: The first president of independent USA was;
explanation_steps: George Washington served as the first president of the United States from 1789 to 1797. He is often referred to as the 'Father of His Country' for his leadership during the American Revolution and the early years of the new nation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** an aim of Italian colonial policy in Eritrea?

options.A: To provide quality education for Eritreans in order to enhance their knowledge.
options.B: To form Italian settlement in Eritrea.
options.C: To exploit natural resources of Eritrea.
options.D: To use Eritrea as a base for further expansion.

explanation_steps: Italian colonial policy followed the principle of 'No education for the native' to prevent the indigenous population from becoming enlightened and challenging colonial rule. They focused on settlement, resource exploitation, and strategic expansion.

questions.stem: Which of the following Pan Africanism Conferences was **unique** in its theme and Participation;
explanation_steps: The 5th Pan-African Congress (often referred to as the Manchester Congress of 1945) is considered unique because it marked a shift from racial solidarity to a demand for absolute independence. It was also the first time that actual African leaders (like Kwame Nkrumah and Jomo Ken

questions.stem: Which Derg’s offensive is known as the **“BahreNegash Campaign”**?
explanation_steps: The Sixth Offensive, also known as the 'Red Star' (Wofri Qeyih Kokob) campaign launched in 1982, was referred to by the Derg as the 'Bahre Negash Campaign'. It was the largest military operation aimed at crushing the EPLF in Nakfa.

questions.stem: Immediate cause for the outbreak of WWII was Hitler invasion of **_______** in $$ 1939 $$.
explanation_steps: The immediate cause of World War II was the German invasion of **Poland** on September 1, $$ 1939 $$. Following this act of aggression, Great Britain and France declared war on Germany on September 3, $$ 1939 $$.

questions.stem: Which of the following was **not** an effect of European exploration?

options.A: Conversion of many people to Christianity.

explanation_steps: All the listed options (A, B, C, and D) were direct effects of European exploration. Therefore, 'None' is the correct choice as there is no incorrect effect listed.

questions.stem: The greatest Mogul emperor was:
explanation_steps: **Akbar the Great** (reigned 1556–1605) is considered the greatest Mughal emperor due to his military conquests, administrative reforms, and policy of religious tolerance which unified India.

questions.stem: The **Sino-Japanese War** was completed with the treaty of ____________.
explanation_steps: The First Sino-Japanese War (1894–1895) ended with the Treaty of Shimonoseki. Under this treaty, China recognized the independence of Korea and ceded Taiwan and the Liaodong Peninsula to Japan.

questions.stem: Which of the following events happened **last** in order?

options.A: Entente Cordiale agreement b/n Britain and France
options.B: Signing of Magna Carta (Charter) in England
options.D: Annexation of Bosnia and Herzegovina by Austria
options.E: Signing of Brest-Litovsk treaty b/n Germany and Russia

explanation_steps:
Chronological order: 
1. Magna Carta (1215)
2. Entente Cordiale (1904)
3. Annexation of Bosnia (1908)
4. Treaty of Brest-Litovsk (March 1918)
5. Foundation of League of Nations (January 1920). 
Therefore, the foundation of the League of Nations happened last.

questions.stem: Native salaried chiefs in highlands served Italians were called ________.
explanation_steps: In the Eritrean highlands (Kebessa), the Italians used the traditional title of 'Mislene' for native chiefs who were incorporated into the colonial administrative hierarchy and received salaries.

questions.stem: The following were Portuguese colonies in Africa **except**;
explanation_steps: Egypt was never a Portuguese colony. It was part of the Ottoman Empire and later came under British influence/protection. Mozambique, Angola, and Guinea-Bissau were all major Portuguese colonies in Africa.

questions.stem: In the 1978 strategic retreat the Derg regime was assisted by;
explanation_steps: During the Strategic Retreat of 1978, the Derg regime received massive military support from the Soviet Union (USSR), Cuba, and South Yemen. This support included advanced weaponry, military advisors, and combat troops, which forced the EPLF and ELF to withdraw from liberated tow

questions.stem: ELM was eradicated by ELF in $$ 1965 $$ at the battle of **_______**.
explanation_steps: The Eritrean Liberation Movement (ELM), also known as 'Haraka', was militarily neutralized by the Eritrean Liberation Front (ELF) in $$ 1965 $$ at the battle of **Ela-Bahel**. This occurred due to tactical and ideological differences between the two organizations.

questions.stem: Mention six **IGAD** member countries?
questions.answer: Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda.
accepted_answers: Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda.
explanation_steps: The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) is an eight-country trade bloc in Africa. The member states are: Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda.

questions.stem: Identify the **wrong** pairing?
explanation_steps: The Tigris and Euphrates rivers are associated with the Mesopotamian civilization, which was primarily located in modern-day **Iraq**, not Iran. While parts of the rivers touch borders, the historical civilization center was Iraq.

questions.stem: Which of the following Bantu kingdoms is well known for its **marvelous stone walls** that were built for the first time in the region?
explanation_steps: **Great Zimbabwe** is famous for its massive dry-stone structures and walls built without mortar between the $$ 11^{th} $$ and $$ 15^{th} $$ centuries.

questions.stem: **Aurangzeb** reign in India during the **Mogul empire** was witnessed in,

options.D: Immense famine and hardship in India.

explanation_steps: Aurangzeb was the last of the great Mughal emperors. His reign was characterized by strict authoritative rule, religious intolerance (reinstating the Jizya tax), constant wars against the Marathas, and economic decline leading to famine.

questions.stem: The idea of Marxism (Scientific Socialism) was formulated by;
explanation_steps: Marxism was developed by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels in the mid-19th century. Their most famous work, 'The Communist Manifesto' (1848), outlined the principles of scientific socialism.

questions.stem: British General who led the war against Italians in Keren on March 27, 1941 was
explanation_steps: General William Platt led the British forces (Sudan Force) from the west into Eritrea. The decisive Battle of Keren ended on March 27, 1941, with the British capturing the strategic town.

questions.stem: Recognized African leader proposed **Regional Union** of African states economically and politically in 1960s was
explanation_steps: Kwame Nkrumah of Ghana was the most vocal advocate for the immediate political and economic unification of Africa (the 'United States of Africa'). He believed that individual African states were too weak to survive alone against neo-colonialism.

questions.stem: Member of the splinter groups severely attacked by the ELF was;
explanation_steps: In the early 1970s, the ELF (Eritrean Liberation Front) leadership declared a 'civil war' against the splinter groups. The Obel group (later known as PLF-1) was one of the primary targets of these attacks as the ELF sought to remain the sole representative of the struggle.

questions.stem: The Book **“Social Contract”** was written in $$ 1762 $$ by **_______**.
explanation_steps: The influential political treatise *The Social Contract* was written by the Genevan philosopher **Jean-Jacques Rousseau**. In it, he argued against the divine right of kings and proposed that legitimate authority comes from the 'general will' of the people.

questions.stem: Mention the contents of **Addis Ababa treaty** in 1896?
questions.answer:
1. Italy recognized the absolute independence of Ethiopia.
2. The Treaty of Wuchale was formally annulled.
3. Italy retained control over Eritrea (the Mareb-Belessa-Muna line was accepted as the border).
accepted_answers:
1. Italy recognized the absolute independence of Ethiopia.
2. The Treaty of Wuchale was formally annulled.
3. Italy retained control over Eritrea (the Mareb-Belessa-Muna line was accepted as the border).
explanation_steps: The Treaty of Addis Ababa was signed on October 26, 1896, following the Battle of Adwa. It ended the First Italo-Ethiopian War. Italy recognized Ethiopia as an independent state and the 1889 Treaty of Wuchale was abolished.

questions.stem: The Upper and Lower Egypt were united in $$ 3100 \text{ B.C} $$ by __________.
explanation_steps: King **Menes** (also identified as Narmer) is credited with unifying Upper and Lower Egypt around $$ 3100 \text{ B.C} $$, becoming the first Pharaoh of the First Dynasty.

questions.stem: The capital city of prophet Mohammed and the four Caliphs was sited in:
explanation_steps: **Medina** (Yathrib) was the political capital of the first Islamic state under Prophet Mohammed and the first three Rashidun Caliphs. Mecca remained the spiritual center.

questions.stem: The members of the **Triple alliance** in 1882 were;
explanation_steps: The Triple Alliance was a secret agreement between Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Italy formed in May 1882. They promised mutual support in the event of an attack by any other great power.

questions.stem: Identify the **early failure** of the League of Nations?

options.A: Danzig became free international city for 15 years.
options.B: Aaland island dispute b/n poles and Finland was solved.
options.C: Took measure on solving Upper Silesia conflict b/n Germany and Poles.
options.D: The League was silent when Japan invaded Manchuria in 1931.

explanation_steps: The invasion of Manchuria by Japan in 1931 was a major failure for the League of Nations. Despite China's appeal, the League failed to take effective action, which weakened its international authority.

questions.stem: Italians simply occupied Eritrea because of;

options.C: Eritreans were fed up of frequent attack by the Abyssinian warlords.
options.D: Italians Killed and imprisoned native elites.

explanation_steps: Italy's expansion into the Eritrean interior was facilitated by internal crises in the region: the 'Kifu Qan' famine (1888-1892), the death of Emperor Yohannes IV at Metemma (1889), and the local population's exhaustion from constant raids by Abyssinian warlords.

questions.stem: The Organization of African Unity (OAU) was transformed into African Union (AU) in 2002. Which African nation is the last to join AU?
explanation_steps: South Sudan became the 54th member of the African Union shortly after gaining independence in July 2011. (Note: Morocco rejoined in 2017, making it the 55th, but it is not listed in the options).

questions.stem: The term **Age of information** refers to,

options.B: The classical societies of the Greco-Roman world.
options.C: The societies of the Renaissance Age in Florence.
options.D: The post industrial societies of the western world.

explanation_steps: The 'Information Age' (also known as the Digital Age) refers to the period in human history characterized by the shift from traditional industry to an economy based on information technology. It is associated with post-industrial societies.

questions.stem: Bahta Hagos revolt took place in the year **_______**.
explanation_steps: Bahta Hagos, the chief of Akkele-Guzay, led a significant revolt against Italian colonial rule in **1894**. He rebelled primarily due to the Italian policy of land alienation (confiscating native lands for Italian settlers).

questions.stem: List the causes of **English bourgeoisie Revolution** in 1642?
questions.answer:
1. Conflict between the King (Charles I) and Parliament over power and taxation.
2. Religious tensions between the Church of England and Puritans.
3. Economic grievances of the rising middle class (bourgeoisie).
4. The King's attempt to rule without Parliament (Personal Rule).
accepted_answers:
1. Conflict between the King (Charles I) and Parliament over power and taxation.
2. Religious tensions between the Church of England and Puritans.
3. Economic grievances of the rising middle class (bourgeoisie).
4. The King's attempt to rule without Parliament (Personal Rule).
explanation_steps: The English Civil War (1642–1651) was caused by a struggle for political supremacy between the monarchy and Parliament, exacerbated by religious disputes and the economic interests of the merchant class.

questions.stem: The writing system that was used in the Mesopotamian Civilization was:
explanation_steps: The Sumerians of Mesopotamia developed **Cuneiform**, which is a wedge-shaped script written on clay tablets. It is one of the earliest systems of writing.

questions.stem: Pick out the **odd one**:
explanation_steps: The **Zulu** people are an ethnic group from **South Africa**, not Egypt. All other pairs correctly match an ethnic group or kingdom with its modern-day location.

questions.stem: **“Declaration of Independence”** that was approved by Second Continental Congress in 1776, was written by,
explanation_steps: Thomas Jefferson was the principal author of the Declaration of Independence. It was formally adopted by the Second Continental Congress on July 4, 1776.

questions.stem: Administrative branch of the United Nations Organizations is;
explanation_steps: The Secretariat is the administrative organ of the UN. It is headed by the Secretary-General and carries out the day-to-day work of the organization.

questions.stem: The following were British colonies in South East Asia **except**:
explanation_steps: Indonesia was a colony of the Netherlands (Dutch East Indies), not Britain. Burma, Sri Lanka (Ceylon), Malaysia, and India were all part of the British Empire.

questions.stem: The first prime minister of independent Zimbabwe won in the 1980 black representation election is;
explanation_steps: Robert Mugabe, leader of the ZANU-PF party, won the first democratic elections in 1980 and became the first Prime Minister of independent Zimbabwe.

questions.stem: Association of South East Asian Nations **(ASEAN)** was established in 1967 in:
explanation_steps: ASEAN was established on August 8, 1967, in Bangkok, Thailand, with the signing of the ASEAN Declaration (Bangkok Declaration) by the founding fathers of Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand.

questions.stem: Massawa was liberated by the EPLF through operation **_______** in Feb, $$ 1990 $$.
explanation_steps: The strategic port city of Massawa was liberated from Ethiopian occupation by the EPLF in February $$ 1990 $$ during **Operation Fenkil**. This operation was a decisive blow to the Derg regime as it cut off their main supply line from the sea.

questions.stem: List the Five Eritrean towns remained under the enemy control in 1977?
questions.answer: Asmara, Massawa, Assab, Barentu, and Adi-Keih.
accepted_answers: Asmara, Massawa, Assab, Barentu, and Adi-Keih.
explanation_steps: By 1977, the Eritrean liberation forces (EPLF and ELF) had liberated almost 95% of Eritrea. Only five major towns remained under the control of the Ethiopian Derg regime: Asmara (the capital), Massawa, Assab, Barentu, and Adi-Keih.

questions.stem: Known Commercial city centers during the **Indus valley** civilization were:
explanation_steps: **Harappa** and **Mohenjo-Daro** were the two largest and most important urban centers of the Indus Valley Civilization (located in modern Pakistan/India).

questions.stem: The reason Historians prefer **primary source** from secondary sources because:

options.A: All secondary sources are not reliable.

explanation_steps: Primary sources are **original** records or evidence created at the time of an event. They provide direct, first-hand accounts, which historians value for their authenticity.

questions.stem: **Boston Tea Party** was happened in the American History in;
explanation_steps: The Boston Tea Party took place on December 16, 1773. It was a political protest by the Sons of Liberty in Boston against the Tea Act imposed by the British government.

questions.stem: Hitler plan to invade Russia during WWII in the code name______.
explanation_steps: Operation Barbarossa was the code name for the Axis invasion of the Soviet Union, which started on June 22, 1941. It was the largest military operation in history.

questions.stem: The **actual** economic policy of Britain in Eritrea was,

options.A: To assist the allied war effort in North Africa
options.B: By promoting employment to Italians to avoid government expenditure.
options.C: To repair the war torn economy of Eritrea.

explanation_steps: During the British Military Administration (1941-1952), Britain followed a 'Care and Maintenance' policy. They used Eritrea's resources to support the WWII effort and tried to minimize administrative costs by keeping Italian bureaucrats in their jobs.

questions.stem: Identify the event **not happened** during the 2nd Phase of the dismantlement of the “federation”?

options.B: Chief Executive elected by Ethiopia rather than by Eritrean Assembly.
options.C: All political parties banned except the Unionists.
options.D: Advent of Tedla Oqubit as Eritrean Head Police Force.

explanation_steps: The banning of political parties (except the Unionist Party) happened very early in the federation period (around 1952-1953), which is considered the 1st phase of erosion. The 2nd phase (1955-1962) involved more direct administrative changes like replacing the flag, the seal, and

questions.stem: The concepts of **“satyagraha”** and **“Ahimsa”** are referred to,
explanation_steps: Mahatma Gandhi developed the philosophy of 'Satyagraha' (truth-force or non-violent resistance) and 'Ahimsa' (non-violence) as the primary tools for the Indian independence movement against British rule.

questions.stem: When and where **Muslim League** was established who was its secretary?
questions.answer: The Muslim League was established on **December 3, 1946**, in **Keren**. Its Secretary-General was **Ibrahim Sultan Ali**.
accepted_answers: The Muslim League was established on **December 3, 1946**, in **Keren**. Its Secretary-General was **Ibrahim Sultan Ali**.
explanation_steps: The Muslim League of Eritrea was one of the most important political parties during the British Military Administration. It was founded in Keren to advocate for Eritrean independence and protect the interests of the Muslim community.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** among the achievements of Chinese civilization?

options.B: Production of sundials and Acupuncture Medicine

explanation_steps: The **Shadoof** (an irrigation tool) was a major achievement of the **Ancient Egyptian** civilization, not China. China is famous for paper, printing, gunpowder, and the compass.

questions.stem: The term ‘Eastern Empires’ collectively referred to:
explanation_steps: In historical and geographical contexts, the 'East' or 'Orient' typically refers to the civilizations and empires of **India, China, and Japan**.

questions.stem: **Helios Centric Theory** (Sun, the center of universe) was proposed by,
explanation_steps: Nicolas Copernicus proposed the heliocentric model in his book 'On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres' (1543), stating that the planets revolve around the Sun, rather than the Earth.

questions.stem: Which of the following event **has no** relation with the Cold War?
explanation_steps: The atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki occurred in August 1945 to end World War II. While they influenced the start of the Cold War, they are considered part of WWII. The other options are direct Cold War events.

questions.stem: The Italian diplomat and **Architect of Wuchale treaty** in 1889 was;
explanation_steps: Count Pietro Antonelli was the Italian diplomat who negotiated and drafted the Treaty of Wuchale with King Menelik II in May 1889.

questions.stem: The first chief executive of the Eritrean government in 1952 was
explanation_steps: Tedla Bairu was elected as the first Chief Executive of Eritrea in 1952 after the establishment of the Federation with Ethiopia. He resigned in 1955 due to pressure from the Ethiopian Imperial government.

questions.stem: Atlantic Charter was drawn up in 1941 by:
explanation_steps: The Atlantic Charter was a joint declaration issued by British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt in August 1941. It outlined the Allied goals for the post-war world.

questions.stem: The Mesopotamian civilization were started by the people:
explanation_steps: The **Sumerians** were the first people to settle in Southern Mesopotamia and are credited with starting the civilization around $$ 3500 \text{ B.C} $$.

questions.stem: What is Capitalism?

options.A: Eco-Political system that encourages public ownership of property.
options.B: Economic system that discourages private ownership of property.
options.C: Economic system based on serf master system
options.D: Economic and political system favored communal ownership of means of production.

explanation_steps: Capitalism is an economic system based on **private ownership** of the means of production and their operation for profit. Options A, B, and D describe socialism or communism, and C describes feudalism.

questions.stem: The head quarter of the **International Court of Justice** is;
explanation_steps: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations. It is located at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.

questions.stem: Iran was under the joint administration of_____and _____during WWII.
explanation_steps: In 1941, Britain and the Soviet Union (USSR) launched a joint invasion of Iran to secure oil fields and ensure a supply route (the Persian Corridor) to the Soviets fighting the Nazis.

questions.stem: External factors that influenced nationalism inside Africa were;

options.A: Missionary education and policies of Britain and France

explanation_steps: African nationalism was fueled by various external factors: education provided by missionaries, the experience of African soldiers in WWII, the UN's call for self-determination, and the solidarity shown at the Bandung Conference.

questions.stem: Immediate after the death of Hamid Idris Awate, the field leadership of ELF was held by,
explanation_steps: After the death of the pioneer Hamid Idris Awate in 1962, Tahir Salem took over the field leadership of the Eritrean Liberation Army (the military wing of the ELF).

questions.stem: Identify the **mismatched** one
explanation_steps: Amilcar Cabral was a revolutionary leader, agricultural engineer, and intellectual from Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde. He led the independence movement against Portuguese colonialism, not a Renaissance painter.

questions.stem: The war fought b/n Britain and France in India from 1756 up to 1763 known as:
explanation_steps: The **Carnatic Wars** were a series of military conflicts in the middle of the $$ 18^{th} \text{ century} $$ in India between the British East India Company and the French East India Company. The Third Carnatic War (1756–1763) was the Indian theater of the Seven Years' War.

questions.stem: Identify the European explorer who **circumnavigated** the World from 1519-1522.
explanation_steps: **Ferdinand Magellan** led the Spanish expedition that achieved the first circumnavigation of the Earth. Although Magellan died in the Philippines, his ship, the *Victoria*, completed the journey in 1522.

questions.stem: Scottish engineer invented **Steam engine** in 1769 was;
explanation_steps: James Watt improved the Newcomen steam engine in 1769, making it much more efficient. His invention was a key catalyst for the Industrial Revolution.

questions.stem: Following the evacuation of Egypt, Britain was in favor of Italian expansion in Eritrea. Why?

options.A: To stop the incessant invasion of Abyssinians in the highlands.
options.B: To gain the vote of Italy in Berlin Conference of 1885.
options.C: To prevent French expansion in the area.
options.D: To prevent re takeover of the area by Egypt.
options.E: To keep power aside from local chiefs.

explanation_steps: Britain encouraged Italy to occupy Massawa in 1885 primarily to block French colonial expansion in the Red Sea region, following the Egyptian withdrawal due to the Mahdist revolt.

questions.stem: One of the following nations **was not** founding member of the Arab League in 1945.
explanation_steps: The founding members of the Arab League in 1945 were Egypt, Iraq, Transjordan, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia, Syria, and Yemen. Libya joined later in 1953, and Kuwait joined in 1961.

questions.stem: Eritrean Patriot credited as ‘Jail beaker of Nakurah’ is;
explanation_steps: Aberra Hailu is famously credited with leading the daring escape from the notorious Nakurah prison (located on the Dahlak Islands) where many Eritrean political prisoners were held by the Derg regime.

questions.stem: Which of the following is happened **first** chronologically?

options.A: Formation of Egypt and Syria as United Arab Republic under Nasser.
options.B: Martin Luther King awarded as youngest Nobel Peace Prize winner.
options.E: Overthrow of king Farook by G.Abdel Nasser.

explanation_steps:
Chronology of events:
1. Overthrow of King Farook (Egyptian Revolution): 1952.
2. Formation of United Arab Republic (UAR): 1958.
3. Foundation of OAU: 1963.
4. MLK Nobel Peace Prize: 1964.
5. Six-Day Arab-Israeli War: 1967.

questions.stem: The **Eastern Cushitic** belongs to:
explanation_steps: The **Afar** and **Saho** ethnic groups are classified under the Eastern Cushitic linguistic group. Nara and Kunama are Nilo-Saharan, while Tigrigna and Tigre are Ethio-Semitic.
questions.topic: Ethnic Groups of the Horn of Africa

questions.stem: The first country took initiative in **Slave trade abolition** was:
explanation_steps: **Britain** was the first major power to take significant steps to abolish the international slave trade, passing the Slave Trade Act in 1807 and using its navy to enforce the ban.

questions.stem: The **causes of 1848 Revolutions** in the Austrian Empire, were:
explanation_steps: The 1848 revolutions in Austria were caused by a combination of social, economic, and political factors, including the desire for liberal reforms (ending censorship), nationalist aspirations of various ethnic groups, and resentment toward the privileges of the nobility.

questions.stem: The aim of Biet-Giorgis Meeting in 1946 was:

options.A: To form a Liberal Progressive Party.
options.C: To bring the Pro-independence and Unionist groups closer.
options.D: To start an armed struggle against Britain.

explanation_steps: The Biet-Giorgis meeting (Wa’ala Biet Giorgis) held in October 1946 was an attempt to reconcile the differing political views of Eritrean leaders, specifically between those favoring independence and those favoring union with Ethiopia.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **wrongly paired**?

options.A: Namidi Asikwe----------editor of ‘West Africa Pilot’ News paper

explanation_steps: All pairs are correct: Nnamdi Azikiwe edited the 'West African Pilot', Marcus Garvey led the 'Back to Africa' movement, W.E.B. Du Bois is known as the 'Father of Pan-Africanism', and Léopold Sédar Senghor was a key figure in the Négritude movement.

questions.stem: Which of the following events was happened **first** in order?

options.C: First EPLF Commando raid in the Asmara Air port.
options.D: Sixth ‘Red Star’ offensive of the Derg regime.
options.E: Proclamation on national service in Eritrea.

explanation_steps:
Chronology of events:
1. Sixth 'Red Star' Offensive (Wofri Qeyih Kokob): Feb 1982.
2. First EPLF Commando raid on Asmara Airport: May 1984.
3. Dismissal of Nadow Command (Afabet): March 1988.
4. Third EPLF Congress: 1994.
5. Proclamation on National Service: 1994.
